en: 6. The Pairs on Volitional Formations (Saṅkhārayamaka) 6.1.
The Section on Designations (Paṇṇattivāra) 6.1.1. The Summary of the Section on Designations (Paṇṇattivāra-uddesa)
Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
There are three formations: the bodily formation, the verbal formation, and the mental formation. Inhalation and exhalation are the bodily formation;
applied thought and sustained thought are the verbal formation; perception and feeling are the mental formation. Excluding applied thought and sustained thought...
All mental states associated with consciousness are formations of consciousness (*cittasaṅkhāra*). 6.1.1.1.
Section on Purification of Terms. 6.1.1.1.1.
Positive Order (*anuloma*).
What is the body? What is the bodily formation?
Is the bodily formation the body?
What is speech? What is the verbal formation?
Is verbal formation speech?
Is consciousness mental formation?
Is mental formation consciousness?
6.1.1.1.2. Negative (Paccanīka) Is it not the body, yet not bodily formation?
Is it not bodily formation, yet not the body?
Is it not speech, yet not volitional formation of speech?
Is it not volitional formation of speech, yet not speech?
Is it not mind, yet not volitional formation of mind?
Is it not a mental formation and not mind?
6.1.1.2. Wheel Section Based on the Purification of Terms (Padasodhanamūlacakkavāra) 6.1.1.2.1.
Positive Order (Anuloma)
What is the body? What is bodily formation?
What is verbal formation?
What is the body? What is bodily formation?
Are volitional formations the mental volitional formation?
Is speech the verbal volitional formation?
Are volitional formations the bodily volitional formation?
Is speech a verbal formation?
Are formations a mental formation?
Is consciousness a mental formation?
Are volitional formations the bodily formation?
Is consciousness the mental formation?
Are volitional formations the verbal formation?
6.1.1.2.2. Negative (Paccanīka):
Is it not the body, yet not bodily formation?
Is it not formations, yet not verbal formation?
Is it not the body, nor the bodily formation?
Is it not the formations, nor the mental formation?
Is it not speech, nor the verbal formation?
Are there volitional formations that are not bodily volitional formation?
Are there speech that is not vocal volitional formation?
Are there volitional formations that are not mental volitional formation?
Is it not mind, yet not mental formation?
Is it not formations, yet not bodily formation?
Is it not mind, yet not mental formation?
Are they not formations, yet not verbal formation?
6.1.1.3. The Chapter on Pure Formations (Suddhasaṅkhāravāra) 6.1.1.3.1.
Positive Order (Anuloma)
Is bodily formation verbal formation?
Is verbal formation bodily formation?
Is bodily formation mental formation?
Is the mental formation the bodily formation?
Is the verbal formation the mental formation?
Is the mental formation the verbal formation?
6.1.1.3.2. Negative (Paccanīka) Is it not bodily formation and not verbal formation?
Is it not verbal formation and not bodily formation?
Is it not bodily formation and not mental formation?
Is it not mental formation and not bodily formation?
Is it not verbal formation and not mental formation?
Is it not a mental formation and not a verbal formation?
This is the section on the indication of designations.
